rationale: Sixth turn: answering the registered applicability gap with a much smaller, legible contrast harness (draft/assurance_gap.rs) that holds every input equal except the Entry type's Snapshot::use_snapshots(). It exercises one responder node through the same legal leader prefix (Prepare, AcceptSync of six entries with decided_idx 6, forwarded Compaction::Trim(6)) and then the same legal Prepare from a node whose decided index is 3 with an older accepted round, which is the message whose handling builds the log update. Run locally first: the non-snapshot case aborts with 'attempt to subtract with overflow' while the snapshot-enabled case completes, so the experiment is submitted to bound the asserted defect with measured evidence rather than leaving the gap open.

scope.description: Two single-node scenarios in one test: a responder replica is driven through a legal leader prefix (Prepare, AcceptSync with six entries and decided_idx 6, forwarded Compaction::Trim(6)) and then receives a legal Prepare with decided_idx 3 and an older accepted round. Everything is held equal except the Entry type: one scenario has Snapshot::use_snapshots() == false, the other true. The outcome of handling that Prepare is reported per case.
assumptions: The messages delivered are the shapes a real leader produces (Prepare, AcceptSync/log_sync, forwarded Compaction::Trim, and a later Prepare from a node whose decided index lags); the responder is a real OmniPaxos instance whose state is produced by those messages rather than set directly.

The three-node configuration is used only for construction; the responder is node 2 and the sender is node 1. No tick, no election and no message routing are involved, so nothing depends on scheduling.

AcceptSync carries sync_idx 0 with a six-entry suffix and decided_idx 6, i.e. the update a leader sends to a peer that has no entries yet; the forwarded Trim(6) is legal because the responder's decided index is already 6.

The state this harness reaches (accepted_idx 6, decided_idx 6, compacted_idx 6, accepted round newer than the preparing node's) is the same state the earlier multi-node experiment reached through real message exchange.
Dev profile with overflow checks enabled, matching the controller's cargo test invocation.
excluded: Release-profile behaviour, the persistent storage backend, and cluster-level consequences after the abort are not measured here.
Only the snapshot/non-snapshot distinction is varied; cluster size, batch size, trim index and quorum are held equal.

experiment.prefix: scenario(case, snapshots) builds one OmniPaxos instance (pid 2, nodes 1,2,3, MemoryStorage behind a shared handle) and then calls, in order: handle_incoming(Prepare{n: (1,1,pid 1), decided_idx: 0, n_accepted: 0, accepted_idx: 0}) so the responder promises at ballot (1,1,pid 1) and enters (Follower, Prepare); handle_incoming(AcceptSync{n: (1,1,pid 1), seq_num: (session 0, counter 1), decided_idx: 6, log_sync: {decided_snapshot: None, suffix: six entries 0..5, sync_idx: 0, stopsign: None}}) so it accepts six entries and records decided_idx 6; handle_incoming(Compaction::Trim(6)) so its decided prefix is compacted. The harness then emits state_reached (accepted_idx, decided_idx, compacted_idx) and finally calls handle_incoming(Prepare{n: (1,2,pid 1), decided_idx: 3, n_accepted: 0, accepted_idx: 6}) inside catch_unwind, emitting log_sync_outcome with outcome, panic message and the three indices. The test runs this twice: case nosnapshot_entry (Entry::Snapshot::use_snapshots() == false) and case snapshot_entry (use_snapshots() == true, a max-value snapshot type).
semantic_changes: No production logic is replaced or patched; the harness only uses the crate's public API and message types.
experiment.responsibility: The contrast isolates which captured component decides the outcome: the core's log-update construction selects its branch from T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() and the deciding node's decided index, and the captured in-memory storage implementation aborts on an index below its trimmed prefix.
experiment.revision_reason: New harness file and a second case: the earlier experiment used a full three-node cluster with a crash-recovered node and non-snapshot entries; this one keeps the same request but adds a snapshot-capable Entry type and supplies the leader prefix directly so the applicability boundary can be measured with the rest held equal.

comparisons.description: Without snapshots, handling the stale node's Prepare completes instead of aborting.
With snapshots enabled, the same request completes, bounding the failure to the non-snapshot configuration.

knowledge.assertion: the snapshot branch is taken only when use_snapshots() is true and decided_idx > common_prefix_idx; otherwise get_suffix(common_prefix_idx) is used with no comparison against the responder's compacted index
